items.name: Portal
items.summary: Its block, drawn into a node somebody else's code owns: an element a script hands over, or a `ref:` handle. When `into:` names another node the block moves there with its nodes and state; `null` keeps it aside until a node comes back; it goes when the page, branch or list item it is written in leaves. parts.detail: Markup, put in as markup. It is **not** sanitised — the name says so — and sanitize(…) is one call away for anything the project did not write itself.

items.example:
state body = "

From the CMS

" Unsafe.Html(sanitize(body))

props.name: animate:
props.meaning: Animation played when the element appears

props.name: exit:
props.meaning: Animation played when the element leaves

props.name: easing:
props.meaning: How the animation is paced — a named easing, or any CSS timing function

props.name: stagger:
props.meaning: Delay added per item of a list, e.g. `50ms`

props.name: count:
props.meaning: How long the number it shows takes to count to a new value, e.g. `600ms`

props.name: shared:
props.meaning: A name this element keeps across a route change, so the browser carries it from one page to the next

props.name: class:
props.meaning: Classes added beside the engine's, from the project's own stylesheets

props.name: ref:
props.meaning: A handle on the element, usable as the element: `ref: nameInput`, then `nameInput.focus()`

props.name: drag:
props.meaning: What it carries when it is picked up — by a mouse moved a few pixels, or a finger held still — and dropped on something with `on receive(d)`

props.name: dragGroup:
props.meaning: Which drops it belongs to: a drag goes only to targets of its own group, so tabs and tree rows stay apart

props.name: dropValue:
props.meaning: What this target is, as a drag sees it: `d.over` in the drag's `on dragmove(d)` and in `on receive(d)`

props.name: dropAxis:
props.meaning: Which way its list runs, for where a drop lands

props.name: dropInside:
props.meaning: A drop on its middle lands inside it — a folder, a container — as well as before or after

props.name: trapFocus:
props.meaning: While true, focus moves into it and Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside; when it turns false or the element leaves, focus goes back where it was

props.name: mount:
props.meaning: Run with the element each time it is made — `mount: (n) => initTilt(n)` — and what it returns is the handle `update:` and `cleanup:` get

props.name: update:
props.meaning: Run with the handle again whenever the state it reads changes: `update: (h) => h.setMax(max)`

props.name: cleanup:
props.meaning: Run with the handle when the element leaves — a route change, an `if` branch, a list item: `cleanup: (h) => h.destroy()`

events.name: click

events.detail: The value changed, on every keystroke

events.detail: Held still for half a second; `p.x`, `p.y` say where. The click it ends with is not a click

events.name: swipe
events.detail: A finger or a pen swept across it; `s.direction` is "left", "right", "up" or "down"

events.name: receive
events.detail: Something with `drag:` was dropped on it; `d.value` is what, `d.position` "before", "after" or "inside"
